watches.name: Dream Watch - Kawari Nuri Urushi Lacquer
watches.description: Dream Watch Kawari Nuri — Hand-Lacquered Urushi Dial Watch from Wajima, Japan The Dream Watch Kawari Nuri is a hand-lacquered urushi watch featuring a dial crafted entirely by master Urushi artists at Taya Shikkiten Lacquerhouse in Wajima, Japan. Available in Green and Red, each dial takes 2.5 years to complete and is released in limited quantity, making this one of the most labor-intensive urushi maki-e watches available today. What Makes Wajima Urushi Dial Different Most urushi watches use the traditional Tsugaru Nuri method, where a marble-like texture is built through repeated lacquer layering and carving. The Dream Watch Kawari Nuri takes a different path: Wajima artisans hand-draw the marble pattern directly over a green urushi base layer, using their exclusive Maki-e technique rather than carving. This is a distinct regional craft signature — Wajima urushi versus Tsugaru urushi — and it's the reason this dial cannot be mass-produced or replicated by machine. Gold Maki-e Detailing: Gold Maki-e 3,6,9 Batton Hour markers The logo is hand-painted in real gold Maki-e lacquer, paired with hand-finished 3, 6, and 9-hour markers. Both sit atop a black urushi base layer, creating depth and contrast that changes character under different lighting — a hallmark of genuine hand-crafted urushi work. Wajima, Japan — 400+ Years of Urushi Heritage Wajima is recognized as one of Japan's premier urushi lacquerware regions, with a craft lineage spanning centuries. Taya Shikkiten Lacquerhouse continues this tradition, applying techniques historically used on fine lacquerware to a wristwatch dial — a rare crossover between traditional Japanese craft and modern horology. Why Only a Limited Quantity Each Kawari Nuri dial takes 2.5 years from start to finish, as the multi-layer lacquering and hand-drawing process cannot be rushed without compromising the finish. Because of this, the Dream Watch Kawari Nuri is released in strictly limited numbers — once a batch sells out, the timeline to produce more is measured in years, not weeks. Kawari Nuri Green vs. Red Green — the base tone the marble pattern is drawn over, giving a more traditional, deep jade-like urushi finish. Red — a bolder colorway that intensifies the contrast between the black base layer and the hand-drawn marble texture.

watches.name: Dream Watch — Aka Fuji Urushi Kindai Maki-e 蒔絵
watches.description: Japan's most sacred mountain. Your wrist. The Dream Watch Aka Fuji Urushi Kindai Maki-e primary is a hand-lacquered timepiece depicting Mount Fuji — Fujisan — rendered on a deep urushi lacquer dial. Each watch is finished by a single Japanese master artisan, working through a process that spans weeks and more than forty individual lacquer applications. The base layer is a hand-lacquered urushi dial made in Echizen, Japan and ontop of the urushi dial is decorated with a silk printing maki-e technique or what we call Modern maki-e/ Kindai Maki-e of Red Mt Fuji or "AKA FUJI." The Maki-e technique: Kindai Maki-e Traditional Maki-e (蒔絵 — "sprinkled picture") is one of Japan's supreme lacquer arts, developed in the Nara period and refined over twelve centuries. The artisan draws the art motif in wet urushi using a brush of just three to five hairs, then immediately dusts 24-carat gold powder across the wet surface. Each layer cures in a humidity-controlled cabinet before the next is applied. The result is a dial with physical depth — light enters the lacquer, travels through its layers, and returns warm and alive in a way that no synthetic coating can replicate. Traditional Maki-e : Prices generally start at $800 and can easily exceed $10,000 for intricate "Taka Maki-e" (raised design) or "Togidashi" (burnished) pieces from master artisans like Namiki or Nakaya Kindai Maki-e is a Way to make Maki-e accessible! Enjoyable by ALL! Kindai Maki-e is a modern adaptation of traditional Japanese lacquerware that uses silk-screening and hand-sprinkled metallic powders to create intricate, affordable designs. Why Mount Fuji? Fujisan (富士山) has been the subject of Japanese art for over a thousand years — from Hokusai's woodblock prints to the oldest Maki-e lacquerware in Japan's imperial collection. As a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Japan's highest peak, it carries layered meaning: endurance, beauty, and the aspiration towards something greater. On a watch dial, viewed in the space between your heartbeat and your next breath, it is exactly right.

watches.name: Aero Nacht - Gun Metal Sterling Silver Edition
watches.description: Introducing the Wancher Aero Nacht Gun Metal edition - a stunning timepiece that combines the sleek design of a fighter jet with the intricate mechanics of a chronograph watch. This edition features a unique twist on the standard Aero Nacht, with a sterling silver-made bezel that has been given two different finishes. The first finish, Brushed Silver, takes the bezel to a new level of visual appeal by brushing it to reveal a more striking silver finish with a rugged, weathered style. This finish is designed to evoke the vintage feel of World War II and capture the essence of the fighter jet's inspiration behind the watch. The second finish, Patin Sterling Silver, is achieved through the anodizing technique, giving the bezel a beautiful matte look. Our hometown of Oita, known as the largest Onsen town in Japan, was the inspiration for this finish. Using the natural hot steam from the hot springs, we were able to create a unique patina effect on the bezel that captures the essence of our hometown's beauty. Overall, the Wancher Aero Nacht Gun Metal edition is a true masterpiece that combines style, function, and inspiration. With its unique bezel and fighter jet-inspired design, this timepiece is sure to make a statement on any wrist. SCROLL DOWN FOR MORE INFORMATION
